items.title: Trainspotting
items.line: Trainspotting opened in the UK on 23 February 1996. Danny Boyle made it for £1.5 million and it took about $72 million worldwide, with Underworld and Blur on the soundtrack.

items.title: Nintendo 64
items.line: The Nintendo 64 reached Japan on 23 June 1996 and North America on 29 September at $199.99, with Super Mario 64 and a thumbstick. Europe had to wait until 1 March 1997.

items.title: Tomb Raider
items.line: Core Design in Derby, England shipped Tomb Raider on the Saturn in Europe on 24 October 1996. Toby Gard's Lara Croft helped it sell over 7 million copies.

items.title: Tamagotchi
items.line: Bandai's Tamagotchi went on sale in Japan on 23 November 1996. About 40 million of the egg-shaped pets sold, and teachers got so fed up that many schools banned them.

items.title: Euro 96
items.line: Euro 96 ran in England from 8 to 30 June. England went out to Germany on penalties after Southgate's miss, and Germany won the final 2-1 with the first golden goal in the tournament.

items.title: Dolly the sheep
items.line: Dolly was born on 5 July 1996 at the Roslin Institute near Edinburgh. The world only heard about the first clone from an adult cell on 22 February 1997.

items.title: Pokémon Red and Green
items.line: Pocket Monsters Red and Green came out on Game Boy in Japan on 27 February 1996, with 151 creatures to catch. North America got Red and Blue on 28 September 1998.
